newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Jan 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Jan 22.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- African Mining Group, which bought 34.9 percent of mining house JCI Ltd last year, may be on shaky ground after Tuesday's announcement that major player Thebe Investments had pulled out four weeks ahead of the deadline to put up the cash for the deal.

- The government and the Democratic Party (DP) played hide and seek on Tuesday over strong indications that President Nelson Mandela had offered Tony Leon, the head of the small liberal party, a cabinet post during a weekend meeting.
- All nine provinces have rejected a commission's recommendations on salaries for local council officials, saying they are unrealistic and cannot be implemented.

- Ministries had been given proper deadlines to implement government's macroeconomic strategy this year, reaffirming the ANC's commitment to the policy, the party's economic transformation head Tito Mboweni said.
- Pre-employment testing for HIV, the virus that causes AIDS, might be prohibited by the end of the year if proposals by a South African Law Commission expert group are accepted.
- The South African Revenue Service said it had paid out more than one million rand after tax to informers so far this fiscal year, for information used in special investigations.
BUSINESS REPORT

- Thebe Investment is withdrawing from the African Mining Group, a consortium of black business and trade union related investment companies buying control of mining house JCI from Anglo American, the group said on Tuesday.
- The government is poised to call in massive farming debts, largely from white farmers, in a move that will open the door to agricultural credit facilities for the disadvantaged.

- The Table Mountain Aerial Cableway, which ferries tourists to the top of the Cape's most famous landmark, might be listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, John Harrison, the managing director of the company said.
- The investigation into alleged insider trading by Grant Thomas, former executive chairman of Malbak, was almost complete but was unlikely to result in prosecution, a police spokesman said.
THE STAR
- Squatter camps just near Johannesburg's wealthy Sandton area have become hell-holes of degradation, shame and fear for hundreds of children who have become victims of rape and sexual abuse.

- Racial tensions within the Truth and Reconciliation Commission began just months after the body was established and might have led to the resignation of at least five people at the TRC's Johannesburg office, sources said.

- While Joe Modise, now defence minister, was leading the armed struggle against apartheid, he had a traitor in his own close family who was working as an agent for the government, the Truth and Reconciliation Commission heard.
SAKE-BEELD

- De Beers and Russia have agreed on a new deal for worldwide marketing of diamonds valued at about 16 billion rand. The agreement is expected to be signed by end-January, according to London's Financial Times, quoting the authoritative Diamantaire newsletter.
- The government is planning important announcements to increase flexibility in the labour market, which will be revealed by President Nelson Mandela, Labour Minister Tito Mboweni said.

- The Johannesburg Stock Exchange's outgoing president, Roy Andersen has hailed as successes under his term the doubling of turnover over the past five years and a surge in the value of shares held by blacks from nothing to 28.5 billion rand over the same period.

- The African Mining Group consortium will go ahead with its bid to take up a 34.9 percent interest in mining house JCI Ltd after the announcement that major player Thebe Investments had pulled out of the deal.
